description.text:
This protocol lets a privileged client such as the DDE display settings
panel organize physical outputs into mirroring groups: one source
output whose rendered content is duplicated to one or more mirror
outputs, so that several screens show the same desktop. This is the
"copy mode" of the compositor, as opposed to the default "extension"
mode where each output shows an independent desktop region.

The protocol exposes a singleton manager global that creates and
tracks treeland_output_group_v1 objects. Each group designates a
single source output and an ordered list of mirror outputs, all
addressed by opaque uuid strings. While copy mode is engaged the
compositor exposes a wl_output only for the source output; mirror
uuids come from treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 instead (see
treeland_output_group_v1 for details). An output may belong to at
most one group at a time, and a group drives copy mode only while
it has both a source and at least one mirror.

The compositor persists the set of groups and their configuration
(name, configured source uuid, and configured mirror uuid list)
across compositor restarts and restores them on startup, so groups
survive reboots and reappear as group_added events on bind; this
lets a privileged client configure mirroring once and have it
reapply automatically later. An output must be connected and
enabled when it is first added to a group (via create_group,
set_source, or add_output); once configured it is kept across
unplug/replug and compositor restart and auto-resumes when the
output returns. The name never changes; the configured source and
mirror list persist until a client changes them with set_source,
add_output, remove_output, or dissolve.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are
to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

A singleton global that creates treeland_output_group_v1
objects and broadcasts the set of existing groups to bound clients.

On bind the compositor emits one group_added event carrying the
name of each existing group, followed by a single groups_done
event, so the client can distinguish the initial dump of
pre-existing groups from later group_added events for groups
created after the bind. When any client creates a group every
other bound client receives group_added for it, and when a
group is dissolved every bound client receives group_removed.
Clients therefore never poll for the group set; they obtain a
group object for a name with the get_group request when they
need to observe or edit that group.

Multiple privileged clients such as the DDE display settings
panel may bind and use the protocol concurrently. Commits from
all clients are applied in arrival order; an output claimed by
one group is rejected for another with the non-fatal
output_in_use failure, so concurrent edits never terminate a
connection and clients may retry or adjust.

Destroy the treeland_output_group_manager_v1 object and
release the client's binding to the manager global.

Existing treeland_output_group_v1 objects are not
affected and remain valid until they are destroyed or the
compositor dissolves the group. The client must destroy each
group object separately; the compositor does not cascade
destruction from the manager.

Create a new treeland_output_group_v1 object with the
given initial source output. An empty source creates
a group with no source; the client adds mirrors afterwards
with add_output and may change the source with set_source,
then commits to apply the changes. Copy mode engages once
the group has both a source and at least one mirror after
commit.

The compositor assigns a unique name to the new group; names
are chosen by the compositor, not by clients. The client
learns the name from the name event, which the compositor
emits on the new group object before any other event. The
name identifies the group in the manager's group_removed
event.

If the source cannot be applied — a non-empty source that
does not identify a connected enabled output, or one that
is already a member of another group — the group is still
created with an empty source: the initial state event
reports an empty source uuid, and the compositor emits an
operation_failed event on the new group object before its
done event, with invalid_output when the uuid does not
identify a connected enabled output or output_in_use when
it is already claimed by another group. The client may
later set a source with set_source or add mirrors with
add_output, then commit to apply them.

On success the compositor broadcasts a group_added event
carrying the new group's name to every other bound client;
the caller learns the name from the name event on its new
group object and does not get a group_added event for it.
Other clients obtain a group object for that name with
get_group.

args.name: source
args.summary: uuid of the initial source output, or empty for no source

description.text:
Create a new treeland_output_group_v1 object bound to the
existing group with the given name, for example a group
created by another client or one whose object the client
has since destroyed. On success the compositor sends the
initial state of the group on the new object: one name event,
one state event carrying the effective source and the full
mirror list in list order, then one done event marking the
end of the initial batch.

The name is the compositor-assigned name reported by the
name event on group objects. If the name is empty, or does
not identify an existing group at the time the request is
processed — for example because the group was dissolved
between the group_removed event and this request — the
object is still created, but it is an invalid group object:
the compositor sends no name event and no state event,
emits an operation_failed event with invalid_name before
the done event, and afterwards rejects every request except
destroy with operation_failed invalid_name. The client
should destroy the object.

On success the returned object is an independent handle:
destroying it does not dissolve the group, and several
clients may hold objects bound to the same group at the
same time.
description.summary: get a group object by name

args.name: id
args.summary: a new group object bound to the named group

args.name: name
args.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the group

description.text:
Emitted when an output group is created by any client. Each
bound client receives this event once per existing group on
bind, and again whenever a new group is created — except for
the client that created the group, which learns the name
from the name event on its create_group return object
instead.

The name argument is the compositor-assigned name of the new
group. A client that wants to observe or edit the group
obtains a group object with the manager's get_group request.

args.name: name
args.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the new group

description.text:
Emitted exactly once, after the compositor has finished
sending the bind-time group_added events for all groups that
existed when the client bound. A client receiving this event
knows it has seen the complete initial set and that any
later group_added is for a group created after the bind.

Emitted when an output group is dissolved, whether because a
client sent the dissolve request or because the compositor
removed it as a whole. Every bound client receives this event
for the group; any group objects that client holds for it
receive a removed event and must be destroyed afterwards.

args.name: name
args.summary: the name of the dissolved group

description.text:
Represents one mirroring group: a source output, identified by
its uuid, whose content is duplicated to an ordered list of
mirror outputs, each identified by its uuid. Output uuids are
never empty; an empty uuid in events represents the absence of
a source.

While the group has both a source and at least one mirror, the
compositor exposes a wl_output global only for the source
output. Mirror outputs have no wl_output while copy mode is
engaged, so clients cannot use wl_output-based protocols
(including treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1, which requires a
wl_output) to identify them; they must instead obtain mirror
uuids from the treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol,
which resolves a zwlr_output_head_v1 to the same uuid. A
configured mirror only loses its wl_output while copy mode is
actually engaged; while the group is inert (no effective source
or no effective mirrors) the mirror retains its wl_output and
behaves as a normal extension output. When copy mode exits —
the last mirror is removed, the effective source becomes empty,
or the group is dissolved — the affected outputs become normal
extension outputs again and their wl_output globals come back.

The group keeps a configured source (zero or one) and a
configured mirror list (zero or more). set_source, add_output,
and remove_output queue changes that take effect only when the
client sends commit. The state event reports the effective
runtime state, not the configured state: a configured source or
mirror whose output is currently unplugged or disabled is
absent from that event but remains in the persisted
configuration, so copy mode auto-resumes when the output comes
back. An output may belong to at most one group at a time; one
already in another group fails with the output_in_use failure.

Pending set_source, add_output, and remove_output requests that
cannot be applied because of transient output state (e.g. an
output unplugged between the request and the commit) are
reported via a non-fatal operation_failed event when the commit
is processed; the group is otherwise unchanged and the client
may retry. Only already_dissolved — sending any request other
than destroy on a dissolved group — is a fatal protocol error.

On creation the compositor sends the current state as one
initial batch: one name event carrying the compositor-assigned
group name, then one state event carrying the effective source
(empty uuid when none is available) and the full mirror list,
followed by one done event marking the end of the initial
batch. If the create_group source was rejected, an
operation_failed event is sent before the done event; for an
invalid group object from get_group the batch is only an
operation_failed event followed by done. Later changes are
reported by further state events; the name never changes.

Several group objects may be bound to the same group, for example
one from create_group and others from get_group; they all
observe the same state. Destroying one
object only releases that client's handle. The dissolve request tears down the group as a
whole, emitting removed to every bound group object and
group_removed on the manager. After removed the object is inert:
only destroy is valid, and anything else is rejected with the
already_dissolved error.

When a member output is unplugged or disabled the compositor
updates the effective runtime state without dissolving the
group: an unavailable mirror is dropped from the mirror list,
and when the configured source becomes unavailable the
compositor auto-promotes one of the available mirrors to the
effective source, reporting its uuid as the source and
dropping it from the mirror list in the same state event.
Clients observe only the effective source and mirror list
carried by each state event and must not assume which mirror
is promoted or whether the promotion outlives the
disappearance of the configured source. To pin a particular
output as the source, a client calls set_source with its
uuid and then commits.

The source uuid is empty only when the group has no available
output at all: no configured source is available (or none is
configured) and there is no available mirror to promote. The
group itself remains. Client-driven remove_output, by contrast,
removes the output from the persisted configuration.

Destroy this group object and release the client's handle.
The group itself is not affected: copy mode continues, other
handles remain valid, and the compositor does not emit
group_removed. Use dissolve to tear down the group as a whole.
It is safe to destroy an object that has already received the
removed event.

Queue the output identified by the given uuid as the
configured source of the group, replacing any current
configured source. The change takes effect only when the
client sends commit. The previous configured source, if
any, becomes a mirror and keeps participating in copy mode
as an effective mirror while its output is available.

If the output is already a member of this group, for
example a current mirror, it is directly promoted to the
source: the compositor pins it as the configured source
and re-resolves the mirror list, which now holds the
previous configured source if it is still available. No
remove_output is required beforehand. If the output is not
a member yet, it joins the group and becomes the source.

If the request cannot be applied at commit time, the
compositor emits an operation_failed event and leaves the
pending change unapplied: invalid_output if the uuid does
not identify a connected enabled output, or output_in_use
if the output is the source or a mirror of another group.

Setting the source again for the output that is already
the current effective source succeeds idempotently and pins
that output as the configured source. This lets a client
pin a particular output as the source.

A later set_source replaces an earlier uncommitted one; the
compositor applies only the most recent source designation
on commit.

args.name: uuid
args.summary: uuid of the output to designate as the source

description.text:
Queue the output identified by the given uuid to be appended
to the end of the group's mirror list at commit time.

If the request cannot be applied at commit time, the
compositor emits an operation_failed event and leaves the
pending addition unapplied: invalid_output if the uuid does
not identify a connected enabled output, duplicate_output
if the output is already in this group, or output_in_use if
it belongs to another group.

args.name: uuid
args.summary: uuid of the output to add as a mirror

description.text:
Queue the removal of the output identified by the given
uuid from the configured membership of the group at commit
time. If the output is not a configured member at commit
time, the compositor emits an operation_failed event with
not_in_group and the removal is unapplied; this covers an
output that was never added as well as one whose
configuration was already removed.

If the removed output is the configured source or a
configured mirror, the compositor re-resolves the effective
source and mirror list as described in the interface
description and reports the result in a state event.

args.name: uuid
args.summary: uuid of the member output to remove

description.text:
Apply all pending set_source, add_output, and remove_output
requests in the order they were queued. Requests that cannot
be applied are skipped, each reported by an operation_failed
event, and the remaining requests are still applied. The
queue is then cleared. If any applied change altered the
effective source or mirror list, the compositor emits one
state event carrying the resulting effective state;
otherwise no state event is emitted.

Sending commit with an empty queue is valid and does
nothing. dissolve discards the pending queue.

Tear down the group: exit copy mode, remove it from the
manager, and release the affected outputs. The configured
source and mirror list are discarded and the group is not
restored on compositor restart. The compositor emits removed
to every group object bound to this group and group_removed
on the manager. After removed the object is inert; only
destroy is valid, and anything else — including dissolve
again — is rejected with already_dissolved.
description.summary: dissolve the group and exit copy mode

description.text:
Reports the name the compositor assigned to this group.
Emitted exactly once on each group object, before any other
event, so the creator of the group learns its name without a
group_added event. The name is unique among existing groups
and never changes; a dissolved group's name may be reused by
a group created later. It identifies the group in the
manager's group_removed event and is the name accepted by
the manager's get_group request.
description.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the group

args.name: name
args.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the group

description.text:
Emitted exactly once on each group object, immediately after
the initial name and state events — or, for an invalid
group object, after the operation_failed event — marking
the end of the initial state batch. A client receiving this
event knows it has the complete initial state of the group
and that any later state event reflects a change. It is
sent even when the initial source is empty and the mirror
list is empty.
description.summary: the initial state batch is complete

description.text:
Reports the current effective runtime state of the group in
a single atomic event: the effective source uuid and the
complete ordered list of effective mirror uuids. The client
replaces any previously known state with the contents of
this event; the source and the mirror list are always
consistent within one emission.

The effective source is the configured source if it is
currently connected and enabled; otherwise it is an
auto-promoted mirror or empty, as described in the
interface description. The mirror list holds the configured
mirrors that are currently connected and enabled, in list
order; the source output, if any, is not part of the list,
and a count of zero means the group has no effective
mirrors.

Emitted once on creation and again whenever the effective
source or the effective mirror list changes: after a
successful commit, and when any member output is unplugged,
disabled, re-enabled, or replugged.

The uuids argument contains the concatenation of count
uuids, one per mirror, in list order. Output uuids assigned
through treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1 are fixed-length
and never contain the NUL byte; the compositor must preserve
this property for every uuid it assigns, and clients may rely
on it to split the array. Each uuid is therefore the array
size in bytes divided by count, and parsing needs no
separators: the client reads count fixed-length uuids back
to back. The count argument always matches the number of
uuids in the array; a client may use it to validate the
array size. The list order follows the order in which
mirrors were added; unavailable mirrors are filtered out
without shifting the relative order of the others.
description.summary: current effective source and mirror list of the group

args.name: source
args.summary: uuid of the current effective source output, or empty when none is available

args.name: count
args.summary: number of mirror outputs in the list

args.name: uuids
args.summary: concatenation of count same-length mirror output uuids, in list order

description.text:
Emitted to every group object bound to the group when the
group is dissolved. After this event the object is inert and
the client must destroy it.

Emitted when a create_group source, get_group, or a
committed set_source, add_output, or remove_output request
cannot be applied, or when a request is sent to an invalid
group object. For a committed set_source, add_output, or
remove_output request the cause is a transient or dynamic
output state, such as an output being unplugged between the
request and the commit or already claimed by another group;
that change is skipped and the client may retry. For a
failed create_group source the group is created with an
empty source and the event is emitted on the new group
object before its done event. For an invalid get_group the
object is invalid, no name event is sent, and every later
request except destroy is rejected with invalid_name. This
is not a protocol error and the connection is not
terminated.
description.summary: a queued or requested change could not be applied

args.name: uuid
args.summary: the output uuid the client passed to the failing request, or empty when the failure is not about an output

description.text: Raised as fatal protocol errors on the group object.

entries.name: already_dissolved
entries.summary: the group has been dissolved; only destroy may be sent

description.text:
Returned by the operation_failed event when a create_group
source, get_group, or a committed set_source, add_output, or
remove_output request cannot be applied, or when a request
is sent to an invalid group object. These reflect transient
or dynamic output state (e.g. an output unplugged between
the request and the commit, or already claimed by another
group), not a protocol violation; the client may retry or
adjust and the connection is not terminated.

entries.name: invalid_output
entries.summary: no enabled output with the provided uuid is currently connected

entries.name: duplicate_output
entries.summary: the output is already a member of this group

entries.name: output_in_use
entries.summary: the output is the source or a mirror of another group

entries.name: not_in_group
entries.summary: the output is not a member of this group

entries.name: invalid_name
entries.summary: the group object is invalid because get_group was given an empty or unknown name
